title: CHO cultivation
scientific_status: Reference evidence and known-baseline reproduction; zero admitted new laws.

findings.title: The spectral correction gives a modest repeatable gain over linear permittivity
findings.evidence: The selected correction reaches 1.6311 million cells/mL experiment-mean RMSE versus 1.7255 for linear permittivity, improving all three reserved pairs. The 5.47% gain misses the frozen 10% practical threshold.

findings.title: Sensor availability and a flexible baseline explain the limits of the proposed mechanism
findings.evidence: An availability-only control reaches 1.6585; the flexible RBF baseline reaches 1.3383. The small incremental spectral gain and negative spectral coefficient do not establish a dielectric cell-size or viability mechanism.

source.publisher: Uhlendorff, Selina (Institute for Life Science Technologies (ILT.NRW), OWL University of Applied Sciences and Arts, Lemgo, Germany); Fulek, Ruwen (Institute Industrial IT (inIT), OWL University of Applied Sciences and Arts, Lemgo, Germany); Eimler, Jonas (Institute for Life Science Technologies (ILT.NRW), OWL University of Applied Sciences and Arts, Lemgo, Germany); Pein-Hackelbusch, Miriam (Institute for Life Science Technologies (ILT.NRW), OWL University of Applied Sciences and Arts, Lemgo, Germany); Frahm, Björn (Biotechnology and Bioprocess Engineering, OWL University of Applied Sciences and Arts, Lemgo, Germany)

applicability: Ninety-two reference rows in experiment pairs EXP005, EXP009 and EXP012, containing six reactors. Current readings use a causal 30-minute summary or a bounded 2-hour carry; source quality flags and the Cole R² threshold remain in force. Offline VCD/SEM are never predictors. Three pairs in this process do not establish external cell-line or manufacturing transfer. The original output-directory recovery changed no model or data.
packaging_change: Only navigation, code representation and packaging changed. No source measurement, fitted parameter, sample selection or admission decision changed.
